a1_subject: Computer's coded character set (correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when a locale is not in effect)
a1_text: Computer's coded character set (correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when a locale is not in effect). This item is required. This item need not be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (15.57, LOWER-CASE function; 15.97, UPPER-CASE function)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 35 'Computer's coded character set (correspondence between lowercase and uppercase letters when a locale is not in effect). This item is required. This item need not be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'This item need not be documented in the implementor' -> OK §A.1 35)). §15.97.4 r4 'When a locale is not in effect, the implementor defines the correspondence of lowercase letters to uppercase letters' -> OK §15.97.4 4); §15.57.4 r4 twin -> OK §15.57.4 4). No documentation obligation, so (a) is waived; CONFORMANCE.md nevertheless states it voluntarily in §3 (DETERMINATION L9, 'the invariant tables', simple one-code-unit-to-one correspondence, ß stays ß). Code: CobolIntrinsics.UpperCase = s.ToUpperInvariant(), LowerCase = s.ToLowerInvariant() - a defined, length-preserving (r5) correspondence; the locale arms (r2/r3) route through CobolLocale. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob: UPPER-CASE('aéß') -> 'AÉß', LOWER-CASE('ÉA') -> 'éa'. Test: conformance:2002/pb64t5_case_locale_phrase line PLAIN - a program with no classification and no phrase maps 'i' -> 'I' (ORD 74) even while LC_CTYPE is Turkish, i.e. r4's implementor correspondence and not the locale's. Caveat for the refuter: the golden pins the UPPER-CASE direction of r4 only; LOWER-CASE r4 is verified by probe and by code reading, not by a golden. Owning note: none (PB738's 'item 35' is Annex E.3.3, unrelated). || REFUTER: UPHELD (CONFORMS). Probes in 85/2002/2014/2023 incl. contained programs, SET LOCALE LC_CTYPE/LC_ALL and LANG/LC_ALL=tr_TR: no locale leaks into the r4 invariant arm (IntrinsicRenderer picks LOCALE-phrase / classification / invariant at compile time); length preserved for ASCII, non-ASCII, national and supplementary-plane arguments. Test-ref widened to the two goldens pinning the LOWER-CASE no-locale arm (pb8 '6=bcd', pb10 'RELEASE-FROM=abcdefgh'); gap noted: no golden pins non-ASCII r4 or LOWER-CASE r4 against a contrasting locale. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535. || editions note: (UPPER-CASE/LOWER-CASE with the r2-r4 locale split; the no-locale mapping applies to every edition that has the functions)

a1_subject: Computer's coded character set (when composite alphanumeric and national, mapping of characters to each)
a1_text: Computer's coded character set (when composite alphanumeric and national, mapping of characters to each). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for a composite alphanumeric and national computer character set. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.2, Computer's coded character set)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 36 'Computer's coded character set (when composite alphanumeric and national, mapping of characters to each). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for a composite alphanumeric and national computer character set. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2 'When these are implemented as one character set, the implementor shall specify the characters that map into the computer's alphanumeric coded character set and the characters that map into the computer's national coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). CONDITION IS MET: CONFORMANCE.md rows DOC-A.1-33 and DOC-A.1-188 state 'Both native repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position' - one coded character set for both classes (§8.1.2 NOTE 2's UTF-16 shape). CONFORMANCE.md has NO '| DOC-A.1-36 |' row stating which characters map into the alphanumeric set. Row 33's 'TOTAL IDENTITY' implies all 65,536 code units are alphanumeric, but the code treats the alphanumeric set as Latin-1 at every byte boundary: probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob - PIC X holding '€' (ORD 8365 in memory) has storage image 0x3F (ByteSub, EC-DATA-CONVERSION only when checked), and a sequential file writes '?' silently (PB690). So the mapping the item demands is both unwritten and not single-valued in the code. Harm: silent (a user cannot learn which characters an alphanumeric item holds losslessly). Owning note: none names item 36 (grep 'DOC-A.1-36\|item 36' hits only Annex E.3.3 item 36 notes PB434/PB438/PB441/PB595); PB690 (open, blocked on owner) owns the file-encoding half and names rows 31/34. Reported as finding charset-determination-unwritten-and-split with 31/38. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535. || editions note: (national coded character set introduced 2002) || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-36 (absent)

a1_subject: Computer's coded character set (whether UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters recognized in class alphanum
a1_text: Computer's coded character set (whether UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters recognized in class alphanumeric; applicable syntax and general rules). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for UTF-8 or mixing alphanumeric and national characters in literals and data items of class alphanumeric. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.2, Computer's coded character set; 8.3.3.2, Alphanumeric literals, Syntax rule 2 and General rule 3)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 38 'Computer's coded character set (whether UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters recognized in class alphanumeric; applicable syntax and general rules). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for UTF-8 or mixing alphanumeric and national characters in literals and data items of class alphanumeric. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.3.3.2.3 SR2 'An implementation is neither required to recognize nor prohibited from recognizing UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters in format 1 alphanumeric literals. When permitted, the capability shall be optionally available to the user ...; the implementor shall specify any applicable syntax rules' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 -> OK §8.3.3.2.3 2)); §8.3.3.2.4 GR3 c) '...the implementor shall specify the applicable general rules' -> OK §8.3.3.2.4 3) c). Code: an alphanumeric literal accepts ANY UTF-16 character, unconditionally (no option): probe cs1.cob 01 A PIC X(3) VALUE '€é' compiles clean at the default std and holds U+20AC. Whether that is 'mixed alphanumeric and national' depends on the item-31/36 determination of the alphanumeric repertoire, which is unwritten and split (UTF-16 in memory per rows 33/188; one byte / Latin-1 at the storage image and on files - ByteSub '?' and PB690). If € is a national character in class alphanumeric, the capability is always on, contrary to SR2's 'optionally available to the user', and its rules are undocumented; if it is alphanumeric, the item's condition fails but the byte boundary contradicts it. Either way the code fixes a behavior and CONFORMANCE.md has no '| DOC-A.1-38 |' row => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note: none names item 38 (PB725's 'item 38' is E.3.3). Clustered into finding charset-determination-unwritten-and-split (31/36/38); PB690 owns the file half. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535. || editions note: (the §8.3.3.2.3 SR2 UTF-8/mixed permission accompanies the national set, 2002+) || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-38 (absent) | src/Cobol.Net.Frontend (alphanumeric literal lexing admits any UTF-16 character)

a1_subject: CONTINUE statement (precision and maximum size of the arithmetic expression specifying the number of seconds to pause ex
a1_text: CONTINUE statement (precision and maximum size of the arithmetic expression specifying the number of seconds to pause execution) This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation (14.9.9, CONTINUE statement, General rule 1).

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 39 'CONTINUE statement (precision and maximum size of the arithmetic expression specifying the number of seconds to pause execution) This item is required. This item shall be documented'. §14.9.9.4 GR1: 'The implementor shall specify the value of m, which may be zero, and the value of n, which shall be greater than zero' (cite.py --check 14.9.9.4 -> OK §14.9.9.4 1)); 'The implementor shall specify the maximum meaningful value of arithmetic-expression-1' -> OK §14.9.9.4 1); 'If the value arithmetic-expression-1 is greater than this maximum meaningful value, the maximum meaningful value is placed into the temporary data item' -> OK §14.9.9.4 1). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-39 |' row. Only m is stated, in §2 A.3 row 8 ('Implementor m = 0 (integer seconds)'); n is stated nowhere and the maximum (CobolTiming.MaxSeconds = 86_400) lives only in a code comment. TWO defects: (1) documentation - missing row (harm silent), owned by PB160 (open: 'CONTINUE item 39 (precision + 86,400 max live only in a code comment)'), referenced not re-reported. (2) NEW, wrong-answer: the maximum-meaningful-value clamp is applied AFTER an unchecked narrowing to long, so an interval beyond 2^63 wraps. StatementEmitter emits '(long)(x.Expr)' (Scale-0 lane) / '(long)(...).ToUnscaled(0, Truncation)' (Dec lane) and SleepTruncated does Math.Min(secs, MaxSeconds) on the already-wrapped value. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/ca2.cob (--std default 2023): 'CONTINUE AFTER 18446744073709551619 SECONDS' suspends ~3 s (wall 5.4 s vs 2.4 s baseline) and 'CONTINUE AFTER 18446744073709551616 SECONDS' suspends 0 s; probe ca.cob with 01 BIG PIC 9(20) VALUE 2^64 likewise returns at once. GR1 requires the maximum meaningful value (86,400 s) to be placed in the temporary for any value above it. The Real (float) lane is safe ((long)double saturates, then Min). No kb/Work note owns the wrap (grep of CONTINUE AFTER notes for wrap/overflow: PB241/PB138/PB463 do not cover it; PB463 is the sibling pattern for SET SIZE OF). Finding: continue-after-interval-wraps-before-clamp. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1529, PB1535. || editions note: (CONTINUE AFTER is a 2023 addition, §14.9.9) || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/StatementEmitter.cs#Visit(BoundContinueAfter) | docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-39 (absent)

a1_subject: DEFINE directive (mechanism for providing value of a compilation-variable-name from the operating environment)
a1_text: DEFINE directive (mechanism for providing value of a compilation-variable-name from the operating environment). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (7.3.11, DEFINE directive, General rule 4)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 49 'DEFINE directive (mechanism for providing value of a compilation-variable-name from the operating environment). This item is required. This item shall be documented ... (7.3.11, DEFINE directive, General rule 4)'. §7.3.11.4 GR4 'If the PARAMETER phrase is specified, the value referenced by compilation-variable-name-1 is obtained from the operating environment by an implementor-defined method when the DEFINE directive is processed. If no value is made available from the operating environment, compilation-variable-name-1 is not defined' (cite.py --check 7.3.11.4 -> OK §7.3.11.4 4)). CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-49 |' row and no mention of the PARAMETER mechanism anywhere (grep 'PARAMETER phrase', '7.3.11'). Code fixes the mechanism: the process environment variable whose name is the compilation-variable-name AS SPELLED in the directive (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name), no case folding); unset -> the name is removed (GR4's 'not defined', met); a value that parses as an invariant-culture decimal is numeric, otherwise alphanumeric. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/def.cob ('>>DEFINE MyVar AS PARAMETER' / '>>IF MyVar IS DEFINED'): no env -> NOT-DEFINED; MYVAR=x -> NOT-DEFINED; MyVar=x -> DEFINED; NUMV=7 -> numeric, '>>IF NUMV > 5' true. So the value source depends on the SPELLING of a case-insensitive COBOL word (MyVar and MYVAR name the same compilation variable but read different environment variables on a case-sensitive host) - a legitimate implementor choice only if documented, and it is not. Harm: silent. Owning notes: none names A.1 item 49 (PB1369 covers items 23/40/53/54 of §7; PB1367 (open) owns the DEFINE general-format / SR2 bypass on the PARAMETER arm, a different defect). New finding: define-parameter-mechanism-undocumented-and-spelling-sensitive. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1533, PB1535. || editions note: (the DEFINE directive, §7.3.11) || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ConditionalCompilationProcessor.cs#ApplyDefine (DefineKind.Parameter arm) | docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-49 (absent)

a1_subject: DELETE FILE statement (effects of the DELETE file statement)
a1_text: DELETE FILE statement (effects of the DELETE file statement). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.10, DELETE statement, General rule 20)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 51 'DELETE FILE statement (effects of the DELETE file statement). This item is required. This item shall be documented ... (14.9.10, DELETE statement, General rule 20)'. §14.9.10.4 GR20 'If the execution of the DELETE FILE statement is successful, the file is deleted if it exists or no action takes place if the mass storage file does not exist' (cite.py --check 14.9.10.4 -> OK §14.9.10.4 20)). The implementor-defined content is what 'the file is deleted' DOES on this platform. CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-51 |' row. Adjacent determinations exist but answer other questions: DOC-A.1-50 (GR19, validated attribute set EMPTY), §3 '⚖ DETERMINATION — the DELETE FILE statement's GR20/GR21 are internally contradictory' (control-flow reading, PB141), §2 row 31 (Claimed). Code fixes the effect (FileRegistry.DeleteFile): a single host File.Delete of the connector's resolved HostPath - no sidecar/index/lock artifact is removed ('NOTHING ELSE IS DELETED, and the absence is the design (kb/Work PB802)'); a bare ASSIGN USING connector with no association yet is '05' without touching any file; presence probed through HostFile.Probe ('05' absent / '37' unauthorized); a file held by another connector or run unit is '62' and not deleted; IOException maps to '37'/'30' (ForDeleteFileFailure). a1_subject: Dynamic-capacity table (determination of highest permissible occurrence number)
a1_text: Dynamic-capacity table (determination of highest permissible occurrence number). This item is required. This item does not have to be documented in the implementor's documentation. (8.4.2.3, Subscripts)

staged_record.notes: A.1 item 60: 'Dynamic-capacity table (determination of highest permissible occurrence number). This item is required. This item does not have to be documented' (8.4.2.3). §8.4.2.3.4 GR2: 'The highest permissible occurrence number for any given dimension of a dynamic-capacity table is implementor-defined and may be affected by the availability of runtime resources. If the value of the subscript is not a positive integer or is less than one or is greater than the highest permissible occurrence number, the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist.' cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.4 'dynamic-capacity' -> OK §8.4.2.3.4 2). No DOC-A.1-60 row (not required; but DOC-A.1-62's cell asserts 'the same ... determination item 60 records for a dynamic-capacity table (CobolDynTable<T>.MaxOccurrences)' — a cross-reference to a row that does not exist). Code: the determination IS fixed — MaxOccurrences = 0x3FFFFFFF; a receiving subscript past it raises EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT (probe: MOVE 1 TO E(2000000000) -> 'EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT (fatal) ... implementor maximum (1073741823)'). Two edges fail: (1) GR2's EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT is never set for a dynamic table — probe with >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON: E(3) at capacity 2 (sending) and E(0) both return the seed '07' with EXCEPTION-STATUS blank, while a fixed OCCURS 5 table's E(0) raises EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT; owned by kb/Work/PB1268 (open, names RefSending/RefReceiving). (2) 'may be affected by the availability of runtime resources': a growth below MaxOccurrences that exhausts memory dies with a raw .NET 'Out of memory.' (probe oom.cob, DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit=2GB, MOVE 'A' TO E(1000000000)) instead of a bounded maximum; owned by kb/Work/PB1410 (open). Editions: OCCURS DYNAMIC is 2014+ (compiler gates it at 85 — char_neg_occurs_dyn85). No spec-derived test pins the maximum itself -> PARTIAL. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1268, PB1410, PB1535.

staged_record.notes: A.1 item 61: 'Dynamic-capacity table (physical allocation). This item is required. This item does not have to be documented' (8.5.1.9). §8.5.1.9.1: 'The size, location, and time of physical allocation of a dynamic-capacity table are implementor-defined.' cite.py --check 8.5.1.9.1 'The size, location, and time of physical allocation of a dynamic-capacity table are implementor-defined' -> OK §8.5.1.9.1 (General). No DOC-A.1-61 row (not required). Code: out-of-line managed array per table instance, allocated at construction (>=4 slots, opened at FROM/VALUE capacity), grown by doubling in GrowTo on demand (capped at MaxOccurrences), shrink by SetCapacity keeps the slots (licensed by the §8.5.1.9.4 NOTE) and GrowTo re-seeds re-created occurrences. The allocation-failure edge is unhandled: Array.Resize's OutOfMemoryException escapes GrowTo uncaught, so a growth the runtime cannot allocate kills the process ('Out of memory.', probe oom.cob under a 2GB GC heap limit) instead of §8.5.1.9.6 GR2's EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT ('higher than the maximum capacity of the table based on the resources available at runtime'); owned by kb/Work/PB1410 (open). Allocation strategy verified by reading; failure path diverges -> PARTIAL. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1410, PB1535.
